question.text: A tube of length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>50</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> is filled completely with an incompressible liquid of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>250</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> and closed at both ends. The tube is then rotated in horizontal plane about one of its ends with a uniform angular velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><msqrt><mi>F</mi></msqrt><mo> </mo><mi>rad</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>F</mi></math> be the force exerted by the liquid at the other end then the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> will be _____ .

solution.text:
Considering an element of tube of length dx having mass dm at a distance of x from right end as shown in figure below.

Now, force acting of that element is F=∫dmω2x

Integrating the above relation for whole length of tube, we have 

 F=∫0LmLdxω2x

=mLω2L22 =mω2L2

⇒ω=2mLF  =20.25×0.5F

=16F=4F rad s-1

Hence, the value of x=4.
